projects.name: Hydra
projects.description:
Hydra picks the model best suited to each task, and can check the answer before you rely on it. It is an open source gateway (the hyctl CLI and a desktop app, written in Go) that discovers the models you can reach, from hosted APIs to local servers and CLI agents, and ranks each on its measured record for the task type. With a target set, a sequential probability ratio test asks models and checkers until per-model calibration says the answer is likely enough to be correct, and asks another model when the check fails.

Beyond routing, Hydra is the accountability layer for agentic development. It enforces PII and local-only policy so sensitive data never leaves the machine, and logs every request with token counts and cost. `hyctl security` answers what the agents on this machine actually did and whether the record can be trusted: a hash-chained tamper-evident MCP ledger, correlated incident detection, OWASP LLM Top-10 coverage, and a governed risk register with SLA clocks crosswalked to NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001 and MITRE ATLAS. `hyctl mcp registry` scores the MCP servers you actually have installed against the CSA MCP Selection Scorecard, known-CVE cross-reference, typosquat detection, and a lifecycle automaton that drops a server back to provisional on every version bump, the direct answer to a server that ships clean for months and then turns malicious.

Every run writes a per-run event trace, model selection, swarm attempts, SPRT samples with the running probability of a correct answer, agent-to-agent handoffs and file edits, which the TUI cockpit and the desktop app replay as a live timeline. Ships as a single static binary for macOS, Linux and Windows.
